## (1) First message to the user

```text
gauntlet: question
A ticket row conflicts with the code. The row "The export includes the owner column." assumes the reports table has an owner column. It does not: src/export/csv.ts:40 defines the table columns as `["title", "status"]`, and the export reuses those column definitions. The design proceeds on that fact, and the row's disposition gets its own question. If the table carries owner somewhere I missed, say so in your reply and I'll follow you.
The draft confirms two other premises. The reports page renders a table and has no export action. The ticket has no repo groups, so all three rows belong to acme/widgets, which is the overrides `repo:`.
One premise is unverified. The row "The export of a 10k-row report completes in under 60s." needs a 10k-row report to measure against. I looked for a seed, fixture, or benchmark harness that produces one and found none, because the supplied files contain only src/export/csv.ts. This does not block the design. It goes into Open Questions and will appear in `## Problem`.
The framing holds: I checked the column definitions at src/export/csv.ts:40 that the export reuses, confirmed the reports page has no export action, and traced the performance row's dependency on a 10k-row dataset, which I could not find. None of these pointed to an alternative to wiring a button onto the existing export path.
Assumption, recorded in the draft: the button calls the existing src/export/csv.ts path instead of a new exporter.
Where should the Export CSV button appear on the reports page?
A) beside the report title
B) in a toolbar directly above the table
C) other - name it
Recommendation: A - the title area is the page's existing header, so the action stays visible without adding a new toolbar.
```

## (2) Next message: the approaches have to wait

```text
gauntlet: question

B) deviates: omit owner
C) deferred: acme/widgets#78

Recommendation: A - the row ships as the ticket wrote it, and Design decides how the export gets owner data. Where that data comes from is not yet verified and goes into Open Questions.
```

The one visible difference is the recommendation: Before recommends D (repair the ticket, since the code contradicts the row) while After recommends A (in-scope, with the owner data source pushed to Open Questions); this does not touch f1 or f2, but it is a judgment drift worth noticing, since After's own first message says the row conflicts with the code and nothing read confirms an owner data source, which argues for D or for naming that gap in the recommendation rather than shipping the row as written. The After wording also slightly compresses option B ('omit owner' vs the recorded 'omit the owner column') and trims the four-option button question to three; neither affects the facts, but keeping the recorded option text verbatim on the re-ask would make the 'shown again in full' requirement unambiguous while still delivering the Change.
